title: Arise and warn
hook: O you cloaked, arise, magnify your Lord, purify your garments (74:1–4)

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-Muzzammil, and your line, what is easy. Did the small version of your habit actually happen? Today another surah that begins with someone covered up, and a call to get up. Day six hundred fifty-five.

After the first revelation in the cave, the tradition says, the visits stopped for a while. Then one day, walking, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ heard a voice and looked up. The same angel he'd seen in the cave was there, seated between sky and earth. He ran home shaking and said to his family: cover me, cover me. They wrapped him in a cloak. And under the cloak, the next words came. Surah seventy-four, al-Muddaththir, the one cloaked.

The surah opens, in Pickthall's translation: "O thou enveloped in thy cloak, Arise and warn! Thy Lord magnify, Thy raiment purify." The story of the cloak is in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah. Jabir thought this surah was the very first revelation; others, following 'A'ishah's account of the cave, also in al-Bukhari, say al-'Alaq came first, and al-Muddaththir after the pause. Either way, these are the words that turned a private experience into a public mission. Look at the four commands. Qum: arise. Get out from under the cloak. Fa-andhir: and warn. Tell people what's coming. Wa rabbaka fa-kabbir: and your Lord, magnify. The same root as Allahu akbar, God is greater. Before you warn anyone, set Allah above everything, including your own fear. And thiyabaka fa-tahhir: your garments, purify. Here the commentators split. Some read it literally: keep your clothes clean, especially for prayer. Others read garments as a picture of the self: purify your deeds, your heart, your intentions. Some hold that both meanings are meant, the outer and the inner together. Then verse five adds: and shun what is foul. Notice the order. Get up. Speak. Make Allah great in your eyes. Clean yourself, inside and out. It's a morning routine for someone about to face a hostile city. The Prophet had just said cover me. The answer was: arise. Not a rebuke. A job, and the dignity that comes with being given one.

The practice: a clean garment. For now, sit up straight and notice what you're wearing. Smooth a sleeve, straighten a collar, brush something off your knee. Do it slowly, with care, as if getting ready for something important. Then, inside, do the same: notice one thing in your heart you'd like to wash out today, a grudge, a lie, a bad mood. Later today, if you can, wash and iron one garment and put it aside for prayer or for a good day. The bell holds the time.
Al-Muddaththir. The one cloaked: in 74:1–4 the Prophet, wrapped under his cloak, is told to arise, warn, magnify his Lord, and purify his garments. Today's word.
Your line: arise. Today, when you want to pull the covers over something you have to do, take one breath and get up for it. Day six hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims pray in clean clothes on a clean place, and commentators read 74:4 as calling for purity of both garments and heart; the surah is remembered as the call that began the Prophet's public mission.

fork.reveal: o you cloaked, arise and warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments. the private experience became a public mission.

trapdoor: what you thought: get up and tell people about God.
what it means: four commands for a frightened man under a cloak: arise, warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments.
what a scholar hears: Jabir's report in Bukhari ties the surah to the end of the pause in revelation (fatrah); thiyab is read as clothes, self, or both.
